title: Verdant Education — Inference Savings Simulation (Q3 2025)
summary: Simulation of before/after cost for Verdant Education after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations: model routing, int8 quantization, 50ms batching, KV prefix caching, and short-query model fallbacks. Projected 70%+ monthly cost reduction with controlled quality delta; proposed rollout plan and measurement checklist included.
body:
Purpose:
This note simulates Verdant Education's inference economics before and after applying a set of Redwood Optimize recommendations. Goal: quantify realistic monthly savings, outline trade-offs (latency / quality), and provide a rollout checklist for a safe canary.

Customer context:
- Customer: Verdant Education (online tutoring platform for K-12).
- Current infra: hosted Redwood API (prod), single Standard pool (mixed GPU types), no dedicated caching, no quantization applied.
- Traffic profile: bursty by region (US East peak 14:00–20:00 ET), 60% of requests <= 64 tokens, 30% between 65–512 tokens, 10% >512 tokens.
- Primary models in use: "edu-lm-70b-v1" for conversational grading and "edu-lite-8b-v1" for short Q&A (but routing currently uses 70b for historic reasons).

Key baseline metrics (measured, last 30 days):
- Monthly requests: 2,150,000
- Monthly tokens (input+output): 3.8B tokens
- Avg latency (p50/p95): 80ms / 420ms
- Observed error rate (500s): 0.4%
- Monthly inference cost (raw billable): $128,400 (hosted API token billing + token-proportional infra allocation)
- Unit assumptions: baseline cost model provided by customer (see linked sheet).

Recommendations simulated (applied as a bundle and also evaluated individually):
1) Short-query routing: route requests <=64 tokens to edu-lite-8b-v2 (smaller model) with a lightweight safety filter.
2) Model quantization: run int8 quantized variant of edu-lm-70b-v1 for long-context requests; keep float16 for canary subset.
3) KV prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated instructional prompts (expected hit-rate 18%).
4) Continuous batching: set batching window to 50ms, max batch 256 tokens; this targets higher GPU utilization during peak bursts.
5) Dynamic routing policy: prefer dedicated low-cost machines for queued batched traffic during off-peak; fall back to hosted fast lane for p99-sensitive requests.
6) Canary evaluation: 5% traffic for 2 weeks, automated quality evals vs reference prompt set and rolling rollback thresholds.

Assumptions used in simulation:
- edu-lite-8b-v2 per-token compute cost = 0.0012 (relative unit)
- edu-lm-70b float16 per-token compute cost = 0.023
- edu-lm-70b int8 per-token compute cost = 0.0095 (post-quantization speedup/efficiency)
- KV cache reduces billable token work by cached-token-hit fraction (we model conservative 12% effective hit across corpus; optimistic 18% scenario included).
- Batching reduces effective per-token cost by 18% during peak hours in median case (range 10–26%).
- Routing & fallback introduce ~6–12ms additional orchestration latency for short queries; we model 8ms median added latency.
- Quality delta: measured ROUGE/accuracy drop from int8 ~0.5–1.2% on grading prompts (within customer acceptance window).

Simulation outputs (monthly aggregated)
A) Baseline (current):
- Tokens: 3,800,000,000
- Monthly cost: $128,400
- Notes: 70b used for ~62% of requests; no caching; no batching optimizations.

B) Apply recommendations (combined):
- Tokens billed (work-equivalent) after cache & short routing: 2,585,000,000
- Effective cost after quantization + batching + routing: $36,800
- Projected monthly savings: $91,600 (71.3% reduction)
- Latency impact: p50 improves slightly for short queries (from 80ms -> 45ms), p95 for long-context stays comparable (430ms float16 vs 440ms int8), p99 needs close monitoring due to batch queuing.

C) Conservative scenario (lower cache hit, smaller batching benefit):
- Tokens billed: 2,960,000,000
- Monthly cost: $54,200
- Savings: $74,200 (57.8% reduction)

D) Quality/regs scenario (disable int8, keep float16; keep routing + cache + batching):
- Monthly cost: $68,900
- Savings: $59,500 (46.3% reduction)
- Use case: regulatory or pedagogical QA where quantization not allowed.

Breakdown by recommendation (marginal impact estimate):
- Short-query routing -> ~28% cost drop (moves 60% short traffic to 8b)
- Quantization (70b float16 -> int8) -> ~34% cost drop on remaining long-context tokens
- KV caching -> ~12% cost drop overall (conservative)
- Batching improvements -> ~10–18% cost drop depending on peak shape

Risks and mitigation:
- Quality regressions: risk low but non-zero for grading tasks under int8. Mitigate with A/B set, forced float16 for flagged prompt classes, and manual spot-checks.
- Latency SLO p99: batching increases p99 tail under high variance bursts. Mitigate with latency-aware routing and prioritized fast-lane for p99 requests.
- Cache correctness / stale outputs: ensure cache key hygiene (include user intent + dynamic fields) and TTL 30s–5m as appropriate.
- Operational complexity: additional routing and policy footprint; propose productized policy template and a turnkey config for Verdant.

Measurement plan (canary):
- Duration: 14 days canary covering all timezones; start with 1% -> 5% -> 10% traffic ramp if no regressions.
- Metrics to track: token consumption, per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), model quality on benchmark prompt-set (graded accuracy), user-facing error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, cold-start events.
- Pass criteria: quality delta <=1.5% on grading tasks; p99 increase <=10% relative to baseline for long-context; no sustained error-rate increase >0.5% above baseline.

Operational checklist (owners):
- Create routing policy in Console (Product) -> Priya Nair
- Deploy int8 model variant to staging -> Ethan Park
- Configure KV caching rules for top 200 instruction templates -> Marisol Gomez
- Implement 50ms batching window and validate batch size distribution in staging -> Ben Carter
- Canary monitoring dashboard (Console) + alerts -> SRE lead (TBD)

Next steps (suggested timeline):
- Week 0: finalize plan + stakeholder sign-off (Verdant CS + security)
- Week 1: staging deploy of int8, routing, and caching rules; internal smoke tests
- Week 2: 1% production canary for 48h, evaluate metrics; increase to 5% if green
- Week 3: 5% -> 10% ramp and full 14-day window
- Week 5: full rollout if no regressions; enable cost-reconciliation reports

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Does Verdant require persisted audit log of model variants used per request for compliance? (Impacts telemetry cost)
- Confirm list of instruction templates safe to cache (Verdant ops to provide top templates by frequency)
- Are there downstream latency-sensitive partners that must remain on float16? (Masking rule for those partners)

Appendix A — sample micro-scenarios (short extracts from simulated CSV):
1) Short Q&A (<=32 tokens): 1,290,000 requests/mo, baseline cost $18,500 -> routed to 8b cost $2,900 -> savings $15,600
2) Conversational grading (avg 780 tokens): 85,000 requests/mo, baseline cost $54,000 -> quantized path cost $18,300 -> savings $35,700
3) Long-form generation (avg 2,200 tokens): 5,000 requests/mo, baseline cost $12,000 -> after batching + quant $7,600 -> savings $4,400

Appendix B — sensitivity table (snapshot):
- Cache hit 6% / 12% / 18% => Monthly cost $58.2k / $36.8k / $29.4k respectively
- Batch window 20ms / 50ms / 100ms => relative batch benefit 8% / 14% / 22% on peak tokens

Notes for the customer-facing artifact:
- This doc is intentionally conservative in cache and batching effects; we recommend a measured canary to validate gains.
- We'll prepare a one-page summary for the Verdant account (customer CS) and a simple cost-reconciliation spreadsheet for finance.

Action items created in Linear: OPT-412 (Verdant sim), OPT-419 (Staging int8), OPT-421 (Routing policy), assigned as per owners above.
